canLinerTypes.name: Traditional Epoxy-Phenolic Resin (BADGE-Based)
canLinerTypes.resinChemistry: Bisphenol A Diglycidyl Ether (BADGE) + Phenol Cross-Linked Network
canLinerTypes.hydrolyticStability: Moderate-Low (Acidic aqueous hydrolysis cleaves ether bonds)
canLinerTypes.lipophilicPartition: Very High (Log Kow = 3.32; readily partitions into oils and animal fats)
canLinerTypes.regulatoryStatus: Phased out in EU food packaging (2024 ban transition); heavily restricted globally
canLinerTypes.description: The historical workhorse of metal packaging since the 1960s. Formed by polycondensation of Bisphenol A with epichlorohydrin. While mechanically resilient, unreacted residual BPA monomer and BADGE hydrolysis chlorohydrins (BADGE·2H2O, BADGE·HCl) migrate into food over extended dwell times, accelerated by heat and acidity.

canLinerTypes.name: Vinyl Organosol (PVC Dispersion + Epoxy Thermal Stabilizer)
canLinerTypes.resinChemistry: High Molecular Weight Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) Dispersed in Plasticizer with BADGE Scavenger
canLinerTypes.hydrolyticStability: High against acids, but releases BPA from thermal epoxy scavengers
canLinerTypes.lipophilicPartition: High (Plasticizers and residual BADGE diffuse into fatty foods)
canLinerTypes.regulatoryStatus: Restricted; subject to migration limits for vinyl chloride and epoxidized oils
canLinerTypes.description: Commonly applied to aggressive tomato products, beverage can ends, and twist-off lug caps due to superior acid flexibility. However, it requires epoxy resins or epoxidized soybean oil (ESBO) as thermal hydrochloric acid scavengers during curing, creating secondary BPA and chlorohydrin migration routes.

canLinerTypes.name: BPA-Non-Intent (BPA-NI) Polyester Coating
canLinerTypes.resinChemistry: Cross-Linked Isophthalic Acid / Terephthalic Acid Polyols (BPA-Free)
canLinerTypes.hydrolyticStability: Moderate (Resilient up to 2 years; susceptible to severe retort blistering if acid pH < 3.2)
canLinerTypes.lipophilicPartition: Low (Negligible lipophilic affinity; zero bisphenol monomers)
canLinerTypes.regulatoryStatus: Compliant with EFSA 2023, FDA 21 CFR 175.300, and California Prop 65
canLinerTypes.description: Modern first-line replacement for epoxy liners. Formulated without bisphenols (BPA, BPS, BPF). Offers good general food barrier properties for vegetables, soups, and beans, though extreme high-acid tomatoes require specialized dual-cure cross-linking to prevent feathering during retort.

canLinerTypes.name: BPA-NI Polyolefin Aqueous Dispersion (POD)
canLinerTypes.hydrolyticStability: Ultra-High (Virtually impervious to citric, acetic, and phosphoric acids)
canLinerTypes.lipophilicPartition: Extremely Low (Non-polar polyolefin backbone blocks oil-phase chemical extraction)
canLinerTypes.regulatoryStatus: Gold Standard Global Compliance (Zero bisphenol or BADGE presence)
canLinerTypes.description: Next-generation aqueous dispersion that deposits a flexible, continuous polyolefin film onto metal coils prior to stamping. Demonstrates zero BPA, zero phthalates, and zero styrene migration, with extraordinary resistance to tomato acidity and aggressive seafood amines.

canLinerTypes.name: Natural Oleoresinous Enamel (Heritage Botanical Resin)
canLinerTypes.resinChemistry: Natural Drying Oils (Tung / Linseed Oil) + Fossil Copal / Ester Gums
canLinerTypes.hydrolyticStability: Moderate-Low (Porous matrix; vulnerable to acid degradation past 12 months)
canLinerTypes.lipophilicPartition: Low (Natural lipid structure, but prone to sulfur staining)
canLinerTypes.regulatoryStatus: BPA-Free Heritage Coating; Approved under FDA 21 CFR 175.300
canLinerTypes.description: Traditional gold-colored enamel formulated from natural plant-derived drying oils. Completely free of synthetic bisphenols. However, it has lower barrier density than synthetic polymers and reacts with sulfur-containing proteins in meats and beans to form unsightly black tin sulfide stains.

canLinerTypes.name: Waterborne Acrylic-Phenolic / Tetramethyl Resin (valPure V70)
canLinerTypes.resinChemistry: Tetramethyl Bisphenol F (TMBPF) / Acrylic Dispersion (Non-Endocrine Disruptor)
canLinerTypes.hydrolyticStability: High (Rigid aromatic network resistant to thermal retort and acid)
canLinerTypes.lipophilicPartition: Low-Moderate (High cross-link density prevents monomer diffusion)
canLinerTypes.regulatoryStatus: Approved by EFSA, US FDA, and French ANSES following multi-generation tox screening
canLinerTypes.description: Engineered by packaging chemists specifically to match epoxy's corrosion resistance without endocrine activity. Methyl groups flanking the phenolic rings prevent binding to estrogen receptors (ER-alpha, ER-beta, ERR-gamma), eliminating hormonal mimicry while resisting harsh canning retorts.

foodMatrixProfiles.name: Crushed San Marzano Tomatoes & Tomato Paste
foodMatrixProfiles.hydrolyticRisk: Severe (High citric and malic acid concentrations promote ether linkage scission)
foodMatrixProfiles.description: High concentration of organic carboxylic acids (citric, malic) at pH 3.8–4.1 aggressively attacks metal-resin interfaces, accelerating hydrolytic scission of cross-linked epoxy chains and extracting unreacted BPA into the tomato matrix.

foodMatrixProfiles.name: Canned Coconut Milk / Cream (Full Fat)
foodMatrixProfiles.hydrolyticRisk: Low Hydrolysis, but Extreme Lipophilic Solvent Extraction
foodMatrixProfiles.description: Rich in medium-chain triglycerides (lauric, myristic acids). Because BPA and BADGE are lipophilic (log Kow ≈ 3.32), fat droplets act as a continuous chemical sink, pulling bisphenol monomers out of the polymer lining into the emulsion phase.

foodMatrixProfiles.name: Solid White / Chunk Light Tuna in Olive Oil
foodMatrixProfiles.hydrolyticRisk: Extreme Lipophilic Extraction into Free Oil
foodMatrixProfiles.description: Free liquid olive oil bathes the inner can wall during 240°F (116°C) pressure sterilization. Lipophilic bisphenols migrate directly into the cooking oil, resulting in 3x to 5x higher BPA concentrations in the oil compared to the drained fish muscle.

foodMatrixProfiles.name: Chunk Light Tuna in Spring Water / Brine
foodMatrixProfiles.hydrolyticRisk: Moderate (Limited lipid partitioning; moderate salt-facilitated migration)
foodMatrixProfiles.description: Dramatically lower lipid content means less lipophilic extraction than oil-packed tuna. However, high protein amine complexes and thermal retort still draw residual free monomers into the water phase.

foodMatrixProfiles.name: Canned Pineapple Chunks / Slices in Heavy Juice
foodMatrixProfiles.hydrolyticRisk: Extreme Hydrolysis (Lowest pH in typical pantry foods)
foodMatrixProfiles.description: With a pH often reaching 3.3–3.5 due to citric and ascorbic acids, pineapple causes rapid chemical attack on lining boundaries, especially along the top lid and bottom double seams.

foodMatrixProfiles.name: Organic Garbanzo Beans / Chickpeas in Water
foodMatrixProfiles.hydrolyticRisk: Minimal (Baseline reference; near-neutral pH and low fat)
foodMatrixProfiles.description: Near-neutral pH (6.2–6.4) with minimal free fat provides the lowest intrinsic leaching environment among canned staples, making it the ideal baseline for migration kinetics.

foodMatrixProfiles.name: Condensed Cream of Mushroom / Chicken Soup
foodMatrixProfiles.hydrolyticRisk: Moderate (Emulsified butterfat and vegetable oils extract bisphenols)
foodMatrixProfiles.description: Emulsified dairy fats and vegetable shortenings create an intermediate extraction gradient, pulling BPA into lipid micelles distributed throughout the viscous starch base.

foodMatrixProfiles.name: Carbonated Cola Beverage in 2-Piece Aluminum Can
foodMatrixProfiles.hydrolyticRisk: High Acidity (Phosphoric acid), but ultra-thin micro-spray lining
foodMatrixProfiles.description: Phosphoric acid drops pH below 2.8, creating a harsh electrochemical environment. However, modern beverage cans use ultra-pure rapid waterborne epoxy-acrylate spray liners that exhibit lower total mass of resin per unit surface than food cans.

canDentProfiles.name: Pristine Undamaged Can (Smooth Body Wall & Flawless Seams)
canDentProfiles.safetyAction: Safe for consumption within labeled shelf-life.
canDentProfiles.description: Factory-perfect cylindrical geometry. The internal polymer lacquer remains uniformly stretched across the tinplate substrate with zero micro-fracturing or localized stress cracking.

canDentProfiles.name: Minor Shallow Body Dent (< 2mm Deep, Away from Seams)
canDentProfiles.safetyAction: Acceptable if can remains hermetically sealed; consume without extended storage.
canDentProfiles.description: A shallow, smooth indentation on the sidewall. Modern coatings possess 10%–15% elastic elongation, allowing the film to flex without full mechanical rupture, though slight localized micro-crazing increases surface area exposure.

canDentProfiles.name: Deep Creased Body Dent (> 3mm Deep with Sharp V-Notch Fold)
canDentProfiles.safetyAction: High risk of chemical contamination and pinhole air entry. Discard recommended.
canDentProfiles.description: Sharp creasing exceeds the tensile strain limit of cross-linked resins, causing the internal lacquer to crack and peel away from the raw steel. Exposed iron/tin sets up a galvanic corrosion cell that leaches tin, iron, and fragmented coating oligomers.

canDentProfiles.name: Double Seam Rim / Chime Dent (Direct Hit to Top or Bottom Crimp)
canDentProfiles.coatingIntegrity: Critical Seam Sealant Compound Failure & Massive Barrier Disruption
canDentProfiles.safetyAction: IMMEDIATE DISCARD: Never consume foods from rim-dented cans.
canDentProfiles.description: The double seam is a microscopic 5-layer interlocking metal fold sealed with rubberized lining compound. A dent here deforms the crimp hooks, crushing the sealant and creating microscopic channels that pull external air, bacteria, and toxic seam sealants into the food.

canDentProfiles.name: Swollen / Bulging Can Ends (Anaerobic Gas or Hydrogen Swell)
canDentProfiles.coatingIntegrity: Catastrophic Coating Failure & Advanced Internal Corrosion
canDentProfiles.safetyAction: LETHAL HAZARD: Do not taste or open. Botulism / Clostridium botulinum neurotoxin or severe acid-iron corrosion risk.
canDentProfiles.description: Bulging lid or bottom indicates positive internal pressure generated either by deadly anaerobic bacterial proliferation (Clostridium botulinum producing lethal botulinum neurotoxin) or severe internal galvanic acid corrosion producing hydrogen gas (H2).

storageConditions.name: Cool Dark Pantry / Root Cellar (15°C / 59°F)
storageConditions.description: Sub-ambient storage decelerates thermodynamic diffusion coefficients and suppresses polymer chain relaxation kinetics according to the Arrhenius relationship.

storageConditions.name: Standard Indoor Kitchen Cupboard (21°C / 70°F)
storageConditions.description: Standard room temperature baseline. Molecular mobility of residual monomers remains within standard FDA and EFSA predictive migration models.

storageConditions.name: Warm Summer Pantry / Non-Air-Conditioned Warehouse (32°C / 90°F)
storageConditions.description: Common during summer months and non-climate-controlled logistics warehouses. Higher thermal energy accelerates ester hydrolysis and doubles monomer diffusion speed.

storageConditions.name: Hot Shipping Container / Car Trunk / Attic Storage (45°C / 113°F)
storageConditions.description: Extreme heat approaches the glass transition temperature (Tg) of certain vinyl organosol and epoxy coatings, triggering massive polymer softening and rapid chemical leaching.

storageDwellTimes.label: Freshly Canned (1 Month Dwell)
storageDwellTimes.description: Short shelf duration; migration limited primarily to immediate surface unbound monomer washout.

storageDwellTimes.label: Moderate Pantry Stock (6 Months Dwell)
storageDwellTimes.description: Standard turnover period for high-volume grocery staples.

storageDwellTimes.label: Full 1-Year Shelf Storage (12 Months Dwell)
storageDwellTimes.description: Reference baseline storage duration used in regulatory migration testing protocols.

storageDwellTimes.label: Aged Pantry Stock (24 Months Dwell)
storageDwellTimes.description: Approaching standard canned food 'Best By' date; cumulative diffusion reaches steady-state plateau.

storageDwellTimes.label: Expired / Hoarded Stock (36+ Months Dwell)
storageDwellTimes.description: Beyond manufacturer date; hydrolytic aging weakens lacquer bonds, facilitating deep core polymer extraction.

consumerProfiles.vulnerability: Critical - Immune Th17 cell dysregulation, allergic sensitization, neurological vulnerability

consumerProfiles.label: Young Child (20 kg / 44 lbs)
consumerProfiles.metabolicPhase: Developing Hepatic Clearance; High Caloric Intake per kg
consumerProfiles.vulnerability: High - Early behavioral, metabolic, and pubertal endocrine disruption risks

consumerProfiles.label: Pregnant / Lactating Individual (65 kg / 143 lbs)
consumerProfiles.metabolicPhase: Maternal-Fetal Placental Transfer & Estrogenic Receptor Susceptibility
consumerProfiles.vulnerability: Extreme - In utero fetal germline epigenetics, mammary gland bud differentiation

consumerProfiles.label: Average Adult (70 kg / 154 lbs)
consumerProfiles.metabolicPhase: Mature Hepatic Phase II Glucuronidation & Renal Clearance (Half-life ~6h)
consumerProfiles.vulnerability: Moderate - Cardiovascular disease association, metabolic syndrome, immune modulation

consumerProfiles.label: High-Intake Adult / Athlete (85 kg / 187 lbs)
consumerProfiles.metabolicPhase: High Metabolic Turnover, Multiple Canned Servings Daily
consumerProfiles.vulnerability: Elevated through Cumulative Dosing (Eating 2–3 cans of tuna/beans daily)

scientificBenchmarks.efsa2023Tdi: 0.2 ng/kg bw/day (European Food Safety Authority Opinion, April 2023)
scientificBenchmarks.efsa2015HistoricalTdi: 4,000 ng/kg bw/day (Previous temporary TDI, revised downwards 20,000-fold)
scientificBenchmarks.fdaHistoricalTdi: 5,000,000 ng/kg bw/day (US FDA 50 μg/kg bw/day reference under active citizen petition)
biologicalMechanisms: Th17 Helper Cell Polarization: Bisphenol A exposure promotes splenic cellular expansion of interleukin-17-producing Th17 cells, exacerbating allergic lung inflammation and autoimmune cascades.

Nuclear Receptor Binding: BPA binds to estrogen receptors (ER-alpha and ER-beta) with 1,000-fold lower affinity than 17beta-estradiol, but binds with nanomolar affinity to estrogen-related receptor gamma (ERR-gamma) and membrane G-protein coupled estrogen receptor (GPER30).
Endothelial Dysfunction: Chronic low-dose dietary BPA impairs nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) phosphorylation, correlated with peripheral arterial stiffness and hypertension.
